messages:
From: Nicholas Barrett <nicholas@pulsehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Amy Lin <amy.lin@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Close Conductor: sequencing MSA/DPA/Order Form for PulseHealth pilot

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement & legal here at PulseHealth are aligning on the pilot procurement timeline. Can you send a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) that sequences the MSA, DPA and order form signings? Our internal target is to have the pilot live by the end of June, but we need the legal milestones and evidence windows to line up with our procurement cadence.

Key asks from our side:
- A short list of required legal signoffs and estimated durations
- Which items must be cleared before we issue a PO
- Any deliverable or acceptance gates that would block go-live

If helpful, I can loop in our procurement lead (Amy) and legal counsel. Would appreciate a draft MAP and any redlines to the MSA you anticipate.

Thanks,

Nicholas Barrett
Director, Procurement
PulseHealth

Attachment: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Nicholas Barrett <nicholas@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close Conductor: sequencing MSA/DPA/Order Form for PulseHealth pilot

Nicholas,

Appreciate the clear asks — attached is a draft MAP (PulseHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx) that lays out milestones for legal review, DPA review, order form finalization and the target deployment window.

High-level sequencing we propose:
1) MSA commercial terms agreed (2–5 business days after initial redline exchange)
2) DPA review (legal-only, parallel to step 1, 3–7 business days)
3) Order form tech/acceptance fields finalized (product/solutions + procurement, 3 business days)
4) PO issuance and counter-signature via DocuSign (1–3 business days)
5) Preproduction/hardening window and acceptance tests (7 days)

Notes & constraints:
- If the DPA needs crypto/HSM language changes, that typically adds a 7–10 day legal loop.
- We can staged-sign MSA and start work under a pilot order form if your procurement can issue a provisional PO earlier — we flagged that option in the MAP.

Marissa (legal) — can you confirm the DPA turnaround assumptions below and flag any clauses that would force a gating delay? Jonas, I copied you for prioritization if we need to compress the timeline.

Next steps:
- Marissa to provide redline summary
- Nicholas to confirm internal PO cadence and whether a provisional PO is acceptable
- We'll produce a version for signature with embedded acceptance criteria

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: PulseHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Nicholas Barrett <nicholas@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close Conductor: sequencing MSA/DPA/Order Form for PulseHealth pilot

Thanks Laura — reviewed the map and added a redline commentary. Attaching a short MSA/DPA redline bundle (MSA_redline_v2.docx) with the items I expect will need negotiation.

Top legal items that could affect sequencing:
- Data residency and subprocessing clauses in the DPA — if PulseHealth requires EU-only residency for analytics, that will require engineering gating and likely delay order form acceptance.
- Liability cap and indemnity language in the MSA — procurement often pushes to escalate these to legal counsel if outside standard thresholds.
- Evidence window for SOC2 reports — we show the window as 5 business days to produce report extracts; if you need longer retention proof we need to scope that.

Suggested flow from legal: prioritize DPA discussion in parallel, but keep the Order Form contingent on agreement to the DPA baseline. If PulseHealth can accept a DPA addendum for the pilot, we can proceed faster.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_redline_v2.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Nicholas Barrett <nicholas@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-21T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close Conductor: sequencing MSA/DPA/Order Form for PulseHealth pilot

Everyone,

Good progress — thanks. From a GTM perspective we should aim to lock a signature cadence this week so engineering can reserve capacity for the pilot window. Two operational asks:

- Nicholas: can procurement commit to a target PO approval date (week of 5/26) so we can plan capacity? Even a provisional PO would let us schedule the onboarding sprint.
- Marissa: if there are high-likelihood escalations on indemnity or residency, flag them now so I can triage with our VP.

If PulseHealth agrees to the provisional PO path (Pilot Order Form + DPA addendum to follow), we can aim for a go-live target of 2025-06-28 with a soft acceptance period the following week.

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

Laura,

Thanks — team is aligned with the MAP approach and the provisional PO route sounds promising. I have two internal constraints:
1) Our Finance approval committee meets 5/28 and we need a clean order form + summary of legal exceptions by then.
2) I can get a provisional PO issued on 5/29 if Marissa's redline summary is narrow; otherwise procurement will need the final DPA.

I've attached our standard procurement cover (PulseHealth_PO_0425.pdf) and would appreciate DocuSign-ready MSA + Order Form PDFs. Can you send DocuSign links and a one-page executive summary for Finance by EOD 5/26? If we can close then, target signature week of 5/29–6/02.

Thanks,

Nicholas Barrett
Director, Procurement
PulseHealth

Attachment: PulseHealth_PO_0425.pdf
